prompt: Here's the current implementation of a per-user "recent activity" feed backed by a Redis list: every new event is written with LPUSH (so index 0 is always the newest), and the feed endpoint reads it back with LRANGE 0 -1. In production some hot user keys have grown to hundreds of thousands of entries, and because Redis executes commands on a single thread, each of these full-list reads now stalls every other client until it finishes — on top of wasting memory forever since nothing ever removes old entries. Walk me through what's wrong with this code, then optimize both the write path and the read path so the feed stays bounded in size and reads stay cheap, while preserving the newest-first ordering the UI depends on.
